method: protobuf check-in with synthetic identifiers, no IMEI

identity_fields.imei: OMITTED — not required, avoids GSMA-space collision

request_shape.credentials: NONE — no Google account, no GSF ID, no tokens sent

side_effects: each probe causes Google to allocate an ephemeral device registration (androidId). This is inherent to the check-in protocol with id=0 and was disclosed to Ray.

fields.has_update: whether the SYNTHETIC fingerprint submitted in this probe is behind the build Google offers for that model+region. The submitted fingerprint is synthetic (placeholder incrementals from prober configs, not real device builds), so this field describes our request, NOT any real device population. Do not report the has_update ratio as a measurement of TECNO's fleet update status.
fields.update_title: the build Google currently offers for this model+region. This is the durable finding — a freshness signal showing what firmware is live at the distribution point right now. Neither FRBox (catalogue) nor naijarom (archive) provides this.
fields.update_url: OTA package URL — NON-DURABLE POINTER, likely signed/session-bound, may not resolve later. Recorded as metadata, NOT fetched. Same treatment as FRBox expired links.
fields.update_description: HTML description of the update (truncated to 500 chars)
fields.unexpected_update_fields: update_* field names present in the response but not in EXTRACT_FIELDS. All 63 rows carry values here — these are Google Play client config knobs (update_clearcut_log, update_download_min_cache_space, etc.) that share the update_ prefix but are NOT OTA metadata.

stripped_fields: update_token — session-scoped bearer token, credential, never stored
androidId — ephemeral registration ID minted by Google per probe, not a device identity
notes: IMEI deliberately omitted from all requests — check-in works without it
update_url is a signed/session-bound pointer that may expire — same treatment as FRBox expired links
Configs from transsion-ota-prober cover 47 TECNO models across ~120 region variants

All 63 rows have unexpected_update_fields content — these are Google Play config knobs sharing the update_ prefix, not OTA metadata. The column works as intended (catching update_* fields not in our extract list); the content is benign.

The fingerprints sent use synthetic incrementals from prober configs (e.g. 135017), not real TECNO builds. has_update=True means our synthetic fingerprint is behind Google's current offering — this is near-tautological and must not be reported as fleet update status.
The durable finding is update_title: the firmware build Google currently distributes for each model+region. This is a freshness signal unavailable from any other source in the corpus.
